text:
The Sabres scratched Ryan McLeod for Friday's win over Columbus, and The Athletic's Matthew Fairburn described it as a wake-up call for the whole room. He was out again in practice Saturday. When a 27-year-old who was worth 1.9 wins above replacement last season (Evolving-Hockey, 58th among 401 forwards) sits in the press box in November, it's a story.

The case against him is easy to make: 3 points in 15 games, 1 goal on 1.72 expected, 0.8 points per 60 minutes. The case for patience is in the luck column. Buffalo has scored 8.6 fewer goals than its chances deserve with McLeod on the ice, one of the biggest gaps we track, and that has cost him points.

He's still elite at getting places: top speed in the 98th percentile, burst speed 97th. Corey Sznajder's All Three Zones tracking from last season has him carrying the puck in on 61% of his entries and making 8.0 primary shot assists per 60 minutes. Evolving-Hockey also noted last year's results ran ahead of his chances, so this may be a correction from both sides. Our projection still says 37 points. We'd expect him back soon.
headline: Ryan McLeod, healthy scratch
